children: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has struck gas at a deepwater well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin, off the Odisha coast, under the Samudra Manthan initiative, the company said on September 18, 2026.
The gas strike was made at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well at a depth of 1,441–1,452 metres. The well was drilled to a target depth of 1,623 metres.

Located around 43 km off Konark, the well is the first drilled by ONGC in the Mahanadi Basin under the campaign. Its proximity to the coast offers potential for early monetisation, subject to further appraisal and commercial evaluation.
The well was spudded on July 25, 2026, by Minister of Petroleum & Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri.

On August 27, ONGC Chairman & CEO Arun Kumar Singh, Director (Technology & Field Services) Vikram Saxena and Director (Exploration) O. P. Sinha visited the drillship Platinum Explorer and interacted with the team engaged in the drilling campaign.
The well has been flowing gas with encouraging flow and reservoir pressure for the last three days, ONGC said.
The discovery strengthens ONGC’s deepwater exploration programme and India’s efforts to expand its indigenous hydrocarbon resource base.
The find, along with other discoveries in the area, can be a candidate for development through shared facilities enabled by the PNG Rules, 2025, bringing deepwater resources onstream.
Oil & Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) shares settled higher at Rs 235.63 per share on the NSE, up 1.22 percent in Monday's trading session.

title: ONGC finds gas near Odisha coast in Mahanadi deepwater basin
